name: Greensleeves
remark: Mutopia Project LilyPond source (public domain, from cyberhymnal, hymn tune 'What Child Is This'), soprano line, E-minor shape (file says key g major but notes use F#/C natural;). Pickup E included (familiar start). Embedded ABC in the same file agrees. Single source, no second cross-check; standard Greensleeves shape.

name: Scarborough Fair
remark: Wikipedia wikitext LilyPond score captioned 'Version commonly used today' (D dorian, 3/4; rest between 'Fair' and 'Parsley' skipped; notes after the rest: A C D). Two thesession.org settings (7522, 18994, E dorian) give the same shape with one fewer repeated note on 'going' (E E B B F# G F# E ...: [0,7,0,-5,1,-1,-2,7,3,2,-2]) or ornamented (E E B A B F# G F# E: [0,7,-2,2,-5,1,-1,-2,0,7,-9]). Traditional ballad PD; this arrangement is the folk-revival tune.

name: Londonderry Air (Danny Boy)
remark: Wikipedia LilyPond score (Eb major, 4/4, pickup D Eb F included, 'Oh Danny boy' text start). thesession.org tune 6867 (The Derry Air, G major: F# G A B A B e d B A G E) gives exactly the same 11 intervals, so two independent notations agree.

name: Skye Boat Song
remark: Wikipedia LilyPond score, 6/8, first line 'Speed bonnie boat, like a bird on the wing' (G G G on 'boat like a'). The second statement of the phrase, and thesession.org tune 3690, use two G's (D E D G G A B A D B A B: [2,-2,5,0,2,2,-2,5,-3,-2,2]); so the start has two settings. Tune PD (Annie MacLeod 1884 / Boulton 1908 arrangement).

name: Loch Lomond
remark: ABC from the Digital Tradition (mirrored in the abc2book corpus), 'By yon bonnie banks', pickup D included; 11 syllables = 11 notes. Setting variants: two other ABC copies (jc 201214820-style, folktunefinder 54021/50523/61779) have B B G instead of B A G on 'and by': D G G A B B G A A G E D [5,0,2,2,0,-4,2,0,-2,-3,-2]; one has an F# ornament pickup. Intervals 1-4 and 7+ are stable across settings. thesession.org 4952 'Loch Lomond' is a different (reel) tune, not used.

name: The Parting Glass
remark: ABC (origin: music.gordfisch.net / folktunefinder 181647, E minor, 4/4), pickup B A included ('Of all the money that e'er I had'). Three other ABC copies (jc 201212613 in G, jc 201322397, folktunefinder 112296) give identical intervals. thesession.org 6275 setting 0 (A minor march, E D C B C A A B ...) is a different, ornamented setting and was not used.

name: She Moved Through the Fair
remark: thesession.org tune 4735 setting 0 (D mixolydian, 3/4) with the opening triplet pickup (3DEF included; first-bar tie A2-A4 merged); setting 17234 (D major) gives the same intervals. Traditional (Colum/Hughes 1909 words by Padraic Colum, tune from Herbert Hughes collection; treat the 1909 Hughes version as PD-age).

name: Auld Lang Syne
remark: Wikipedia LilyPond score (F major, 4/4, pickup C included: 'Should auld acquaintance be forgot'). thesession.org 12441 settings give the same up to note 8 and then an ornamented bar-2 end (B>A: D G G G B A G A B A G G, [5,0,0,4,-2,-2,2,2,-2,-2,0]); setting 20766 has G F# G B at the start. Plain melody used as primary.

name: Kalinka (Larionov)
remark: ABC from the folkinfo collection (BBC Singing Together 1975, K:G but E-minor mode) = the slow verse 'Kalinka, kalinka, kalinka my dear'. The fast refrain 'Ah you garden' (Michel Bellon / folktunefinder 102659, Am: E D B C D B C D C B A E) gives [-2,-3,1,2,-3,1,2,-2,-1,-2,7] (leading E is a held pickup, included). Larionov 1860 tune is PD; this arrangement's tune is the traditional-style melody.

name: Korobeiniki
remark: thesession.org 13747 setting 0 (G major shape of the A-minor tune; = the Tetris 'Type A' melody E B C D C B A A C E D C B..., setting 1 in D minor identical). IMPORTANT: Wikipedia's wikitext score for Korobeiniki (A minor: E G# B G# E A C E D C B C) differs after the opening: [4,3,-3,-4,5,3,4,-2,-2,-1,1], and the klezmer 'Korobushka' ABC (abc2book jc/allklez/89, Bm: F# A# C# A# F# B C# D C# B C# D) gives [4,3,-3,-4,5,2,1,-1,-2,2,1]; so avoid BOTH shapes. Folk tune PD (Nekrasov poem 1861); Tetris arrangement is not.

name: Ochi chornye (Dark Eyes)
remark: ABC transcribed by Frank Nordberg for musicaviva.com (G minor, 3/4) from folktunefinder 151450; opening pickup C# D included; rests skipped (rest between the two 'E D D' groups and before D G). Melody (Hermann 1840s) PD. Single source.

name: Hej Sokoly
remark: Read from the Wikimedia Commons score image (D minor, 4/4, 'Hej tam gdzies z nad czarnej wody', first bars D F D F | A. A G F | E G E G | Bb. Bb A G) and cross-checked by parsing the Commons MIDI File:Hej Sokoly.mid (melody track notes D F D F A A G F E G E G Bb Bb A G), identical. Traditional Polish/Ukrainian-Cossack tune, PD.

name: Palastinalied (Walther von der Vogelweide)
remark: Jack Campin's medieval-song ABC (runabc nmodes.abc, X:40 'Palestine Song / Nu alrest leb ich mir werde', D dorian, 3/4, hexatonic reading). Uncertain: X:280 of the same file (4/4, pickup A) gives A D D F F D D E F E D D [-7,0,3,0,-3,0,2,1,-1,-2,0], i.e. no E after the second F. Rhythm and exact first notes of medieval melody are an editorial reconstruction; melody is c.1204 (PD).

name: Stella splendens (Llibre Vermell)
remark: Michel Bellon's ABC from the Llibre Vermell de Montserrat (G, 2/2); the F-major copy (folktunefinder 40202: D D C D Bb G Bb C Eb D Bb C) and the thesession.org polka 10159 (B B A B G E G A c B G A) give identical intervals, so three notations agree. No pickup. Medieval melody PD.

name: Saltarello (Add. 29987, first saltarello)
remark: Norbeck's collection 'Saltarello' (labelled 14th century Italian, E dorian, 2/4); first 2 notes G A are the pickup into the repeat (they only appear as an ABC anacrusis mirroring the first-ending), skipped. The Dead Can Dance-derived ABC (jc 201333749, 'Saltarello', no pickup) gives identical intervals B E B E B E B A F# G A G. Absolute octaves as written (B down to E, E up to B: +-7); the real melody may spell the same pitch classes with fourth leaps (+-5): treat as interval classes +-5/+-7. Not verified against the manuscript facsimile.

name: Wild Mountain Thyme / Will Ye Go Lassie Go (verse)
remark: Verse 'Oh the summer time is coming' as in folktunefinder 51102/51369 (G, 4/4) and jc 201360967 (D): identical in 3 copies. The chorus 'Will ye go lassie go' starts G E D D E G G G B D E D [-3,-2,0,2,3,0,0,4,3,2,-2] (jc 201212396 'A17', thesession.org 10655/23161, norbeck 2752); the song may be sung from either. PUBLIC DOMAIN: not established - Francis McPeake claimed the 1957 song/arrangement (copyright, died 1971 so UK PD only from 2042); the tune is related to Tannahill's 'The Braes o' Balquhidder' (1810) but the shape here is the McPeake version. Treat as not PD.

name: Katyusha (Blanter 1938)
remark: thesession.org 14315 setting 1 (A minor: A B C A C C B A B E B C) and the Wikifonia ABC of Matvei Blanter's score (wikifonia-dataset/original-abc/MatveiBlanterKatyusha.abc, 'All Rights Reserved', E minor shape) give identical intervals; thesession setting 0 is a variant ('cd/c/ BA' gives A B C A C D C B A B E B [2,1,-3,3,2,-2,-1,-2,2,-7,7]). NOT PUBLIC DOMAIN in many places (Blanter d. 1990): interval shape only.
